Plot releases

Source: R/plot.R
dig_plot.Rd

Plots the counts from dig_tally() with a title, a subtitle that says what is shown, and alt text for screen readers. Genres, styles, formats, labels, artists, roles and countries are drawn as ranked lollipops with the count and share at each tip. Decades are columns with their counts, years are columns with the busiest year marked, and by = "added" is a line of the running total. Plotting needs the ggplot2 package.

Usage

dig_plot(
  x,
  by = c("genre", "style", "format", "label", "artist", "role", "country", "decade",
    "year", "added"),
  n = 10,
  unique = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A tibble returned by one of the functions listed in Details.

by

What to count by: "genre", "style", "format", "label", "artist", "role", "country", "decade", "year" or "added", the month a copy was added.

n

The number of values to keep for all but years, decades and months. The rest are counted together as "Other". Inf keeps all values.

unique

If TRUE, each release counts once, however many copies of it there are.

Value

A ggplot object, which can be changed with +, or NULL invisibly if x is NULL.

Details

The colours have a contrast of at least 3:1 with the background, and every value that is not on an axis is written next to its mark, so no value depends on colour alone. The title, subtitle and alt text can be changed with ggplot2::labs().

Every plot has the caption "Data provided by Discogs.", which the API Terms of Use require next to any data from 'Discogs'. Where you publish a plot, link the caption to the 'Discogs' page with the data. Plots of a collection or wantlist show Restricted Data, see dig_collection().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && rlang::is_installed("ggplot2")
collection <- dig_collection("username", all = TRUE)
dig_plot(collection, "decade")
dig_plot(collection, "added")
dig_plot(dig_artist_releases(1, all = TRUE), "role")
}
